full_judgment:
11. As regards the submission of the learned Advocate for the defendants that claims in the suit as arc sought to be proved by photostat copies of disbursement accounts and vouchers cannot be decreed without proof of the claims by production of the account books and other cogent evidence relating to the disbursement and the freights received by the plaintiff, the learned Advocate has submitted that the alleged revenue receipts against expenses are not supported by any evidence and that the freight manifests of the cargo carried by the ship does not show the freight collected. It is true that except the statement of accounts showing the revenue earned from the freight in the voyages, there is no other evidence to show that the freight earned as shown in the {statement of accounts and disbursement bills and vouchers are correct. 

 14. As regards the other issues, I have noticed that the defendant No. 6 being a party interested in the ship as a purchaser of the ship, namely United Liner Corporation Ltd., hereinafter referred to as the purchaser has alleged that the ship has been sold to him on 23-12-1982, i.e. before the filing of the suit in this Court and as such no decree can be passed against the defendants since there is no maritime lien on account of the claim made by the plaintiff in this suit. The purchaser has also alleged that by obtaining an order of arrest of the vessel he is entitled to a compensation for loss of earning at the rate of US $ 1,500 per day. In support of his case that he has purchased the ship on 23-12-82 i.e. before the suit was filed, the defendant has examined DW 2, the Managing Director of the purchaser Company. It is curious to notice that the DW 1 who is allegedly a Director of the defendant No. 3, the owners of the vessel, is a brother of defendant No. 2, the Managing Director of the purchaser, the United Liners Corporation Ltd. I have also noticed that both the seller, i.e. defendant No. 3 and the purchaser of the ship, defendant No. 6 are represented in the trial by the same lawyer. In my view the transaction of sale of the ship in the facts and circumstances smacks of collusion. In this connection, firstly I may mention that after the institution of the suit on 13-3-83, an application for attachment of the ship was filed by the plaintiff and thereupon an order of attachment of the ship was passed by the Admiralty Court on that date, which was duly served upon the ship, the Master of the ship the owners of the ship being Uniship Ltd. SA Panama. 

 26. For the reasons stated above, the suit succeeds and the plaintiff is entitled to a decree as prayed. In the result, the suit is decreed for US $ 29,511.57 equivalent to Taka 7,13,294.63 with costs.
